nodes.subject: point-and-shoot camera category
nodes.object: automatic snapshot-oriented operation for people who may not consider themselves photographers

support_spans.exact_quote: A point-and-shoot camera , also known as a compact camera and sometimes abbreviated to P&S , is a still camera (either film or digital ) designed primarily for simple operation.
They are popular for vernacular photography by people who do not consider themselves photographers but want easy-to-use cameras for snapshots of vacations, parties, reunions and other events.

accepted_phrases: The point-and-shoot category is designed primarily for simple operation and easy snapshots by non-photographers, often with automatic systems. This is design intent, not proof that an exact old or bundled unit is easy and reliable for the intended recipient.

nodes.subject: self-selection bias
nodes.object: responders may differ from nonresponders for reasons tied to joining the group

support_spans.exact_quote: In statistics , self-selection bias arises in any situation in which individuals select themselves into a group , causing a biased sample with nonprobability sampling .
It is closely related to the non-response bias , describing when the group of people responding has different responses than the group of people not responding.

accepted_phrases: Self-selection can make a participating group differ from nonparticipants or nonresponders. This limits transfer from page reviewers to all buyers or this mother, but it does not prove that any particular review or aggregate is false.

nodes.object: intended users perform intended tasks rather than merely state opinions

support_spans.exact_quote: Usability testing is a technique used in user-centered interaction design to evaluate a product by testing it on users.
Usability testing usually involves systematic observation under controlled conditions to determine how well people can use the product.

accepted_phrases: Usability testing evaluates a product by testing and systematically observing users performing tasks. It supports a mother-operated camera and transfer trial; it does not supply a result for any captured camera in advance.

nodes.subject: image quality
nodes.object: subjective and objective assessments can disagree and require declared outputs

support_spans.exact_quote: Another definition refers to image quality as "the weighted combination of all of the visually significant attributes of an image".
Image quality can be assessed using two methods: subjective and objective.

Objective and subjective methods aren't necessarily consistent or accurate between each other: a human viewer might perceive stark differences in quality in a set of images where a computer algorithm might not.

accepted_phrases: Image quality can concern visually significant attributes and can be assessed subjectively or objectively, with possible disagreement. A comparison therefore needs declared screen or print output, size and task rather than an undefined universal quality label.

nodes.subject: optical aberration
nodes.object: real optical systems can blur distort or fringe an image

support_spans.exact_quote: In optics , aberration is a property of optical systems, such as lenses and mirrors , that causes the image created by the optical system to not be a faithful reproduction of the object being observed.

Aberrations cause the image formed by a lens to be blurred, distorted in shape or have color fringing or other effects not seen in the object, with the nature of the distortion depending on the type of aberration.

accepted_phrases: Optical aberrations can make a lens image blurred, distorted or color-fringed. This explains one legitimate enthusiast test dimension but cannot diagnose an exact seller unit or prove that every inexpensive compact has a soft lens.

nodes.subject: shutter lag
nodes.object: including focus and metering lag and therefore relevant to timing moving subjects

support_spans.exact_quote: In photography , shutter lag is the delay between triggering the shutter and when the photograph is actually recorded, which includes all lag between when the shutter button is pressed and when the photo is taken, including metering and focus lag.
it can be mitigated to an extent by pre-focusing and readying for action.

accepted_phrases: Shutter lag is the delay between triggering and recording a photograph, including focus and metering lag, and can matter for moving grandchildren. The page provides no exact lag or failure rate for a captured unit.
